Model extraction may appear as broad systematic probing, repeated boundary-focused queries, unusually high coverage, or account coordination. These signals also occur in legitimate evaluation, accessibility, and bulk integration, so combine them with authenticated usage context rather than making accusations from query volume alone. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.05820) [2](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)

Apply documented quotas, anomaly review, credential controls, and response minimization appropriate to the product. Track quality/cost impact and false positives, with an escalation path for legitimate high-volume clients. Watermarking or fingerprints can supply additional evidence but are not perfect ownership tests. Avoid returning unnecessary internal logits or training information. Monitoring can raise the cost of extraction; it cannot guarantee prevention when an API intentionally exposes enough useful input–output behavior for imitation.
